summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as an inter-VLAN router between node2 and node3, which each sit in their own subnet behind it. node1's eth1 (192.168.10.1/24) faces node2's enp8s0 (192.168.10.2/24, VLAN A) and eth2 (192.168.20.1/24) faces node3's enp8s0 (192.168.20.2/24, VLAN B). IPv4 forwarding was enabled globally and per-interface on node1, and static cross-VLAN routes were added on node2/node3 via NetworkManager (persistent). node2 and node3 now ping each other across the VLAN boundary via node1 (confirmed by ttl=63, one router hop). All config was made persistent: node1 via a custom systemd oneshot service ([REDACTED].service) that reapplies interface IPs/forwarding after the native SONiC interfaces-config/networking services run, and node2/node3 via NetworkManager connection profiles. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (native `reboot`), each polled back to availability with a changed boot_id proving an actual restart (not just a service bounce), and post-restart checks confirmed the routed interfaces, forwarding sysctls, static routes, and end-to-end cross-VLAN ping all recovered automatically without any manual reconfiguration.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 network interfaces and identified unused NICs (node1 eth1/eth2, node2/node3 enp8s0) as the VLAN-facing links
Performed SONiC pre-config cleanup on node1 (stripped docker0 240.127.1.1/24, flushed eth1/eth2)
Assigned 192.168.10.1/24 to node1 eth1 and 192.168.20.1/24 to node1 eth2; verified direct L3 reachability to node2/node3
Enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward, per-interface forwarding, and disabled rp_filter on node1
Configured node2 enp8s0 (192.168.10.2/24) and node3 enp8s0 (192.168.20.2/24) via nmcli static profiles after discovering NetworkManager reverted plain `ip addr add`
Added static cross-VLAN routes on node2 (192.168.20.0/24 via 192.168.10.1) and node3 (192.168.10.0/24 via 192.168.20.1) via nmcli
Verified end-to-end cross-VLAN ping node2<->node3 through node1 (ttl=63)

Persisted node1 config via /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf and a new [REDACTED].service systemd oneshot ordered after networking.service/interfaces-config.service; verified networking.service was not left masked (would have broken eth0 management access)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially via native `reboot`, polling each until exec access returned and confirming boot_id changed each time
Re-verified routed interfaces, forwarding sysctls, static routes, and end-to-end cross-VLAN ping after each restart

boot_id, interface config, forwarding sysctls, and cross-VLAN ping captured on all three nodes pre-restart

evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from 96974ac3... to 124d50f5...; post-restart enp8s0 IP, route, and cross-VLAN ping to node3 recovered via NetworkManager profile
